description: Share a single keyboard and mouse between multiple computers.

summary.one_liner: Deskflow is a free, open source app that shares one keyboard and mouse (or trackpad) across multiple nearby computers, like a software KVM without video.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you use one computer's keyboard, mouse, or trackpad to control other computers and move between them. The README says TLS encryption is on by default, Wayland is supported on Linux, and clipboard sharing is supported. It is network compatible with Synergy 1, Input Leap, and Barrier, per the FAQ, with Deskflow 1.17.0.96 or later. Packages are offered for download, through a Homebrew tap on macOS, or via build from source. The README points to a wiki page for build instructions.
use_cases: share one keyboard and mouse between computers
control a second computer from my desk
use keyboard and mouse on Linux Wayland desktop
encrypted input sharing over a LAN
how_to_run: Download a package from the project's releases
On macOS: brew install deskflow (stable) or brew install deskflow-dev (continuous)
On Linux: install deskflow from your package repository, or use flatpak
Build from source using the Building wiki page
On Windows, install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable first
notable: Wayland support through libei and libportal
Network compatible with Synergy 1, Input Leap, and Barrier
Clipboard sharing is a core feature
Continuous builds available via Homebrew deskflow-dev
caveats: macOS builds are unsigned and may need xattr -c to run; macOS needs accessibility access granted
Some features may be unavailable or broken on Wayland
Synergy 3 is not compatible; Lan Mouse compatibility is not yet available
keywords: use one mouse on two computers
